objective_for_doctor: Assess and diagnose the patient presenting with sudden loss of vision in one eye.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

Doctor: Hello, I’m your doctor today. What brings you in today? Patient: Earlier today, while I was watching TV, I suddenly lost vision in my right eye—completely and without any pain—and it happened about 30 minutes ago.
Doctor: I’m sorry you’re experiencing that. Can you tell me if you noticed any flashes of light, new floaters, or a curtain‑like shadow before the vision loss started?
Patient: No—I didn’t notice any flashes, floaters, or any curtain-like shadow beforehand. It was just sudden, complete loss of vision in my right eye.
Doctor: Have you experienced any pain in or around the eye, any headache, scalp tenderness, jaw pain while chewing, or any recent fever or systemic symptoms?
Patient: No pain around the eye, no headache, and no jaw pain when chewing. I also haven’t had any recent fever or other systemic symptoms.

Doctor: Do you have any known medical conditions such as high blood pressure, diabetes, high cholesterol, heart disease, atrial fibrillation, or a history of blood clots, and are you taking any regular medications?
“Doctor, I have coronary artery disease, high blood pressure, and type 2 diabetes, and I’m not great at taking my medications regularly.”
Doctor: Do you currently smoke cigarettes or use any other tobacco products, and if so, how many packs per day or how much overall?
Patient: I don’t smoke cigarettes or use any tobacco products. I’ve mainly been struggling to take my blood pressure and diabetes medications consistently.
Doctor: Is the vision loss still present,
Patient: Yes, the vision loss in my right eye is still present and hasn’t improved since it started about 30 minutes ago.
Doctor: Have you ever had any brief, transient episodes of vision loss or “gray‑out” in either eye before this event?
Patient: No, I haven’t had any brief episodes of vision loss or gray-out in either eye before this.
[DDX] Central retinal artery occlusion, Central retinal vein occlusion, Retinal detachment, Anterior ischemic optic neuropathy, Vitreous hemorr
